<reason>Side A won a competitive debate by making eligibility the decisive clash: open sale offers equal terms even if wallets differ, while a meaningful reserved share is a first claim by paperwork. A answered pressure on the lottery/wealth symmetry more cleanly, showed reciprocity does not track disruption or need, and kept remainder-price costs live. Side B was coherent on bounded community recognition and empty loyalty without stock, but never fully justified why outsiders should bear a first-round privilege that can still go to wealthy locals.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2: dynamic sale keeps one eligibility list, while the local/member lottery awards cheaper seats to an in-group first—breaking PRO’s symmetry between wealthy locals and wealthy general-sale buyers.</best_rebuttal>
